preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner
Attacker must hold some amount of the CoinToken to exploit tax manipulation

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, set buy/sell taxes to 100% to steal all tokens from users. First, call setBuyTax(100,0,0,0) and setSellTax(100,0,0,0) to set maximum taxes. Then set tax wallets to attacker-controlled addresses using setTaxWallets(). Finally, trigger tax collection via triggerTax() or have users trade tokens to collect all funds into attacker wallets.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The CoinToken contract allows the owner to set arbitrary tax rates (0-100%) and configure tax wallet addresses. By setting taxes to 100% and pointing tax wallets to attacker-controlled addresses, any token transfers will be fully taxed and sent to the attacker. The triggerTax() function can force tax collection without needing actual trading.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner. 2. Set buy and sell taxes to 100%. 3. Set tax wallets to attacker addresses. 4. Create a victim user with tokens. 5. Have victim trade to generate taxes. 6. Trigger tax collection. 7. Profit from stolen ETH.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate owner. 2. Call setBuyTax(100,0,0,0) and setSellTax(100,0,0,0). 3. Call setTaxWallets with attacker addresses. 4. Create victim address and give tokens via deal. 5. Have victim approve and swap tokens via Uniswap to generate sell tax. 6. Call triggerTax() to collect accumulated taxes. 7. Check attacker ETH balance increased.

attempts.feedback: EVM Revert: CoinToken: Tax is already enabled。请调整参数或调用路径。

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has tax enabled by default (taxStatus = true). With 100% tax, any swap would result in 0 tokens to swap, causing revert. Need to use slightly lower tax rate (99%) to allow swap to proceed while still stealing most funds.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Use 99% taxes instead of 100% to allow swaps to proceed. 2. Remove enableTax() call since tax is already enabled. 3. Give victim ETH for gas and swap. 4. Have victim swap tokens to generate sell tax. 5. Trigger tax collection.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Impersonate owner. 2. Set buy/sell taxes to 99%. 3. Set tax wallets to attacker addresses. 4. Give victim ETH and tokens. 5. Victim approves and swaps tokens. 6. Trigger tax collection. 7. Check attacker balances increased.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because: 1. Tax is already enabled by default, so enableTax() call reverts. 2. With 100% tax, the victim's swap would fail because after tax deduction, amount becomes 0, causing the swap to revert. 3. Need to ensure victim has ETH for gas and swap.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The owner's token balance might be insufficient. We should use Foundry's deal() cheatcode to directly set victim's token balance instead of transferring from owner. This bypasses the need for owner to have tokens.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Use deal() to give tokens directly to victim. 2. Remove the transfer from owner. 3. Keep the rest of the exploit the same.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use deal(TARGET, victim, amount) to give tokens to victim. 2. Remove the owner transfer and exclude logic. 3. Proceed with victim swap.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because the owner doesn't have enough tokens to transfer to victim. The owner's balance might be less than 10,000 tokens after initial setup. Need to use deal() cheatcode to directly give tokens to victim instead of transferring from owner.
